Flags:
      --agent string                 Agent for the distill step (used only with --distill) (default "auto")
      --budget int                   Cap on gated agent runs for the LIFE OF THIS PROCESS (distill + seed); 0 = unlimited. It never resets, so on a long-lived daemon --budget 1 means one run EVER, not one per window — the durable per-window guard is --distill-every + the persisted cursor. Use it only for a bounded foreground run.
      --consolidate-every duration   Minimum interval between full consolidations (heavy refresh); the per-tick short-term delta covers freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every change; a full short-term buffer always consolidates (default 30m0s)
      --distill                      Run distill (SPENDS TOKENS) when new sessions land — gated by --distill-every + --budget
      --distill-every duration       Minimum interval between gated agent runs (distill and/or seed synthesis) (default 24h0m0s)

      --once                         Run a single pass and exit (no daemon loop)

content.content:
Pause background brain work on this machine until `start`.

From its next pass every watcher, installed or run by hand, idles, memory
workers exit without working, the session-end hook skips its refresh and
distill, and `setup` skips its backfill. A pass already running, such as a
`setup` backfill (capped at --backfill-budget sessions), finishes first.

Nothing is lost: captured sessions stay canonical and are picked up by the
watcher, the next hook, or a re-run `setup` once `start` lifts the pause.

Usage:
  entire-brain stop [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for stop

# Vue Corpus

Two realistic Vue applications with a hand-written ground truth. Each app has an
`expected.json` that lists the symbols and relations a correct graph contains,
and tags every fact with the gap it measures. `vue_corpus_test.go` builds a
snapshot of each app, scores it against `expected.json`, and ratchets the
result in `score.json`, so every Vue improvement shows up as facts gained per
tag and every regression fails the test.

```sh
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus' -v            # score and compare
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -update  # record a new score
```

| App | Dialect |
|---|---|
| `taskboard/` | Vue 3, TypeScript, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia, vue-router, composables, `@/` path alias |
| `helpdesk/` | Options API, JavaScript, Vuex modules, mixins, event bus, global registration, kebab-case tags |

The apps are never built or run. They contain no `node_modules` or lockfiles,
and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.

## Manifest Format

```json
{
  "app": "taskboard",
  "symbols": [
    {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone", "kind": "function", "line": 31, "tag": "script-symbols"}
  ],
  "absent_symbols": [
    {"file": "src/App.vue", "name": "selectedId", "tag": "false-elements", "why": ":task-id=\"selectedId\" is a prop binding, not an HTML id"}
  ],
  "relations": [
    {"type": "IMPORTS", "from": {"file": "src/App.vue"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts"}, "tag": "script-imports"},
    {"type": "CALLS", "from": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts", "name": "toggleTask"}, "tag": "store-members"},
    {"type": ["CALLS", "ACCESSES"], "from": {"file": "src/views/BoardView.vue", "name": "BoardView", "kind": "component"}, "to": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "TaskCard", "kind": "component"}, "tag": "template-edges"}
  ]
}
```

- `symbols[].line` is the line that declares the name. A symbol matches when a
  snapshot symbol in that file has the same name, the same kind if `kind` is
  given, and a range that contains `line`.
- `absent_symbols` lists symbols a correct graph must not emit. The name must
  appear in the file, so the trap is real.
- A relation endpoint is a file (`file` only), a symbol (`file` and `name`,
  optionally `kind`), or an external package (`external`, such as `"pinia"`).
  `type` is one relation type or a list of acceptable types.
- Every named endpoint also appears in `symbols`, so the manifest checks itself.

## Tags

Each tag maps to a gap in the Vue gap analysis (G1 to G8) or to a construct the
analysis did not cover yet.

| Tag | Gap | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | | Facts inside plain `.ts`/`.js` files. These work today and must stay at 100%. |
| `script-symbols` | G2 | Functions, consts, and classes declared in `<script>` or `<script setup>` |
| `script-imports` | G3 | IMPORTS from a `.vue` file to `.ts`, `.js`, or `.vue` files |
| `script-calls` | G3 | CALLS from a script function to an imported function |
| `component-owner` | G4 | CONTAINS from the component to its script symbols, and top-level setup calls attributed to the component |
| `false-elements` | G5 | HTML-id false positives that must not appear |
| `template-edges` | G6 | Template event handlers to script functions, and component tags to the component they render |
| `options-api` | G7 | `methods`, `computed`, `watch`, and lifecycle hooks as symbols |
| `store-members` | G8 | Calls through store instances, destructured members, Pinia actions, and Vuex `dispatch`/`commit` strings |
| `path-alias` | new | `@/` imports resolved through the `tsconfig.json` or bundler alias |
| `lazy-imports` | new | `() => import('./X.vue')` routes and `defineAsyncComponent` |
| `global-registration` | new | `app.component` / `Vue.component` registrations used as tags elsewhere |
| `ts-types` | new | Types from `.ts` files used in `.vue` files (`defineProps<Props>()`, typed refs, typed params) |
| `mixins` | new | Components that use a mixin, and calls to mixin members through `this` |
| `event-bus` | new | EMITS and LISTENS_ON through a shared event bus |
| `tests` | new | TESTS from spec files to the composables, stores, and components they cover |
| `script-src` | new | `<script src="./x.js">` external script blocks |

and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.

## Manifest Format

```json
{
  "app": "taskboard",
  "symbols": [
    {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone", "kind": "function", "line": 31, "tag": "script-symbols"}
  ],
  "absent_symbols": [
    {"file": "src/App.vue", "name": "selectedId", "tag": "false-elements", "why": ":task-id=\"selectedId\" is a prop binding, not an HTML id"}
  ],
  "relations": [
    {"type": "IMPORTS", "from": {"file": "src/App.vue"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts"}, "tag": "script-imports"},
    {"type": "CALLS", "from": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts", "name": "toggleTask"}, "tag": "store-members"},
    {"type": ["CALLS", "ACCESSES"], "from": {"file": "src/views/BoardView.vue", "name": "BoardView", "kind": "component"}, "to": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "TaskCard", "kind": "component"}, "tag": "template-edges"}
  ]
}
```

- `symbols[].line` is the line that declares the name. A symbol matches when a
  snapshot symbol in that file has the same name, the same kind if `kind` is
  given, and a range that contains `line`.
- `absent_symbols` lists symbols a correct graph must not emit. The name must
  appear in the file, so the trap is real.
- A relation endpoint is a file (`file` only), a symbol (`file` and `name`,
  optionally `kind`), or an external package (`external`, such as `"pinia"`).
  `type` is one relation type or a list of acceptable types.
- Every named endpoint also appears in `symbols`, so the manifest checks itself.

## Tags

Each tag maps to a gap in the Vue gap analysis (G1 to G8) or to a construct the
analysis did not cover yet.

| Tag | Gap | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | | Facts inside plain `.ts`/`.js` files. These work today and must stay at 100%. |
| `script-symbols` | G2 | Functions, consts, and classes declared in `<script>` or `<script setup>` |
| `script-imports` | G3 | IMPORTS from a `.vue` file to `.ts`, `.js`, or `.vue` files |
| `script-calls` | G3 | CALLS from a script function to an imported function |
| `component-owner` | G4 | CONTAINS from the component to its script symbols, and top-level setup calls attributed to the component |
| `false-elements` | G5 | HTML-id false positives that must not appear |
| `template-edges` | G6 | Template event handlers to script functions, and component tags to the component they render |
| `options-api` | G7 | `methods`, `computed`, `watch`, and lifecycle hooks as symbols |
| `store-members` | G8 | Calls through store instances, destructured members, Pinia actions, and Vuex `dispatch`/`commit` strings |
| `path-alias` | new | `@/` imports resolved through the `tsconfig.json` or bundler alias |
| `lazy-imports` | new | `() => import('./X.vue')` routes and `defineAsyncComponent` |
| `global-registration` | new | `app.component` / `Vue.component` registrations used as tags elsewhere |
| `ts-types` | new | Types from `.ts` files used in `.vue` files (`defineProps<Props>()`, typed refs, typed params) |
| `mixins` | new | Components that use a mixin, and calls to mixin members through `this` |
| `event-bus` | new | EMITS and LISTENS_ON through a shared event bus |
| `tests` | new | TESTS from spec files to the composables, stores, and components they cover |
| `script-src` | new | `<script src="./x.js">` external script blocks |

content.text:
No existing test walks `testdata/` broadly. The relation corpus only reads `fixtures/` and `langmatrix/`, and the git guard skips `testdata` entirely. So the new apps can't affect other tests.

So far, on branch `vue-corpus` (nothing committed):

- **`internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/README.md`** is the spec. It defines the `expected.json` format and 17 tags. Each tag maps to a gap from the analysis (G2 to G8) or to a new Vue construct: `@/` aliases, lazy route imports, global registration, TypeScript types in props, mixins, event buses, tests, and `<script src>`.
- **`internal/sem/vue_corpus_test.go`** is the harness. It has two tests:
  - `TestVueCorpusManifestMatchesSource` checks the ground truth itself. Every symbol must appear on its stated line, every trap must exist in source, and every relation endpoint must be a listed symbol.
  - `TestVueCorpusScore` builds a snapshot of each app and scores it by tag. It ratchets the result in `score.json` with the existing `-update` flag. It fails if any `baseline` fact (something emitted today) is missing.

Two agents are building the apps in parallel, each with 200 to 300 tagged facts:

- **`taskboard`:** Vue 3, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia in setup and options styles, vue-router lazy routes, composables, typed `defineProps`, `defineModel`/`defineExpose`, provide/inject, global components, `@/` alias, vitest specs.
- **`helpdesk`:** Options API JavaScript, Vuex namespaced modules with `dispatch`/`commit`/`mapActions`, mixins and `extends`, an event bus, `Vue.component` with kebab-case tags, `<script src>`, a pug template, jest specs.

When they finish, I'll review both manifests, run the self-check and the scoring, and record the first `score.json`.

content.text:
I built the two Vue apps on branch `vue-corpus` as a scored test corpus. Each app comes with a hand-written list of what a correct graph should contain. Every Vue fix to `entire graph` now shows up as facts gained per gap, and any regression fails a test. All corpus tests pass, and the existing golden-snapshot, capability, and relation-corpus tests still pass. Nothing is committed.

| App | Style | Files | Facts | Found today |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `taskboard` | Vue 3, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia (both styles), vue-router, composables, typed props, `@/` alias, vitest | 56 | 306 | 104 |
| `helpdesk` | Options API JavaScript, Vuex modules, mixins, event bus, `Vue.component`, `<script src>`, jest | 64 | 316 | 102 |

The facts found today are essentially the ones that already work, such as plain JS/TS code and component symbols. Every Vue-specific category is at 0 except one lazy import and one trap. The largest targets are Options API members (52), template edges (49), store calls (41), `<script setup>` symbols (40), and event emits and listeners (36).

**How it works**
- Each app's `expected.json` lists symbols, edges, things that must *not* appear (fake HTML-id elements, false edges), and a gap tag for each.
- `TestVueCorpusManifestMatchesSource` checks the lists against the code, so they can't drift from it.
- `TestVueCorpusScore` scores a snapshot of each app by tag and records the result in `score.json`. After a Vue fix, run it with `-update` to record the gains. `VUE_CORPUS_VERBOSE=1` lists every missing fact.
- The spec and tag list are in `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/README.md`.

**New provider bugs the apps surfaced** (all recorded in the README):
- **False edges:** every Vuex getter and mutation "calls" the module's `state()` function (35 edges). `dispatch('auth/…')` is reported as an event. API helpers that call `get('/path')` are reported as route handlers.
- **Missed imports and calls:** multi-line and aliased imports don't resolve, calls between functions nested in a composable are missing, and `@/` imports via `jsconfig.json` or into `.vue` files from `.ts` become externals.
- **Dropped or missing edges:** lazy imports with a `webpackChunkName` comment are dropped, and test files get no TESTS edges.

I added the clear-cut cases as scored facts under two new tags, `js-resolution` and `false-relations`.

**Decision for you:** I took "distilled" to mean the apps reduce to precise, scored test targets. If you meant `entire brain distill`, that extracts memories from recorded sessions, not from code. Brain is also paused since you turned it off, so I didn't build Brains for these apps. I can do that if you want to view them in `brain viz`.

I can commit this as one change. Opening the PR is yours as usual.

Build a React twin of a Vue test-corpus app so we can measure, construct by construct, how much more of the code graph `entire graph` (a Go code-graph provider) extracts from React than from Vue.

## Inputs (read them first)
- Vue app: `/Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/taskboard/`: Vue 3, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia, vue-router, composables. Its `expected.json` is a hand-written ground truth of ~306 facts (symbols, relations, absent traps), each tagged with a gap category. The README one level up explains the format and tags.
- Comparison tool: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/be8c9437-53d5-4e9f-bb9b-0907a051322f/scratchpad/tools/compare_twins.py`. Read its docstring. It maps every Vue fact to your twin through `twin-map.json` and scores both snapshots. Do not edit it; report problems instead.
- Provider binary built from the repo: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/be8c9437-53d5-4e9f-bb9b-0907a051322f/scratchpad/corpus-check/entire-graph`. Vue snapshot: `.../scratchpad/corpus-check/taskboard.ndjson`.

## Build the twin at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/be8c9437-53d5-4e9f-bb9b-0907a051322f/scratchpad/twins/taskboard-react/`
Only write inside that folder (the scratchpad is shared with other agents).

React 18 + TypeScript. Mirror the Vue app file for file: every `src/**/X.vue` becomes `src/**/X.tsx` with the same component name; plain `.ts` modules (api, types, utils, event bus, router helpers) keep their paths and stay as close to verbatim as React allows; keep `tsconfig.json` with the `@/*` path alias and a `vite.config.ts` alias, `package.json` (react, react-dom, react-router-dom, zustand, vitest, @testing-library/react), `index.html`. Keep every component, function, hook, store action, type and handler NAME identical to the Vue app, and keep the same call structure, so each Vue fact has an obvious React counterpart. The goal is that only the framework differs, not the code shape:
- `<script setup>` top-level functions -> functions declared inside the component function, same names. Top-level setup calls (`useTaskStore()`, `useRouter()`, composables) -> the same hook calls at the top of the component. `computed` -> `useMemo`; `watch` -> `useEffect`; `ref` -> `useState`/`useRef`.
- Template child tags and `@click="fn"` / `@submit.prevent="fn"` -> JSX elements and `onClick={fn}` / `onSubmit={fn}` with the same handler names.
- Typed `defineProps<Props>()` -> `function TaskCard(props: Props)` or destructured props typed with the same imported types. `defineEmits` / `emit('task-moved', x)` -> a callback prop (`onTaskMoved(x)`), and the parent passes `onTaskMoved={onTaskMoved}`. `defineModel` -> value + onChange props. `defineExpose` + template ref -> `forwardRef` + `useImperativeHandle` exposing the same function names.
- Pinia setup-style stores -> zustand stores that keep the same internal shape: `export const useTaskStore = create<TaskState>()((set, get) => { async function addTask(...) {...} ... return { ..., addTask } })`, same function names, same nested calls (for example `moveTask` calling `findTask`). The options-style Pinia store (auth) -> a zustand store whose actions are object shorthand methods (`login() {...}`) with the same names and the same `this`/`get()` calls. Components call actions the same ways the Vue app does: via the store instance, via destructuring, and via a selector.
- Composables -> hooks with the same names and returned functions.
- vue-router -> react-router-dom v6 in `src/router/index.tsx` with `lazy(() => import('@/views/BoardView'))` routes, the same `authGuard` function used by a guard component or loader, `useNavigate()` in place of `useRouter().push`. `defineAsyncComponent` -> `React.lazy`.
- provide/inject with an InjectionKey -> `createContext` / `useContext` with the same key/context names defined in the same `.ts` file location (it may become `.tsx` if needed; record that in `files`).
- Globally registered components (`app.component('BaseButton', ...)`) -> explicit imports in each user; same component names.
- Vitest specs -> the same spec files and test targets using `@testing-library/react`.
- Real static HTML ids may stay in JSX; attribute traps are irrelevant in React.

## twin-map.json (in the twin root)
`{"vue_ext": ".tsx", "files": {...}, "names": {...}, "no_counterpart": {...}}`. List every fact key that has no React counterpart in `no_counterpart` with a one-line reason; get the keys with `python3 -I .../tools/compare_twins.py --keys /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/taskboard`. Keep `no_counterpart` honest and minimal: a construct that exists in React with different syntax is NOT no-counterpart (rendering `<TaskCard>` is a render in JSX too; `@click` is `onClick`). Expected no-counterpart facts include component custom-event EMITS/LISTENS_ON edges (React uses callback props, not channels), HTML-id traps (`false-elements`), and `document` symbols. Use `names` only when React forces a different name, and `files` only for paths other than the default `.vue` -> `.tsx` swap.

## Validate
1. Snapshot: `.../scratchpad/corpus-check/entire-graph snapshot --repo <twin dir> --worktree --format ndjson > .../scratchpad/twins/taskboard-react.ndjson`
2. Compare: `python3 -I .../tools/compare_twins.py /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/taskboard .../scratchpad/corpus-check/taskboard.ndjson .../scratchpad/twins/taskboard-react .../scratchpad/twins/taskboard-react.ndjson --details .../scratchpad/twins/taskboard-details.json`
3. Fix until the tool reports zero MAPPING ERRORS. Do not change the twin's code to chase a better React score; mirror the Vue shapes faithfully and let the numbers fall where they fall.

## Final report (under 350 words)
The comparison table as printed, the no_counterpart count by tag with the main reasons, and the most important observations: for each tag where React scores well and Vue scores zero, what React edge exists; for tags where React also scores low, what the shared failure is (inspect `taskboard-details.json` and the React snapshot to explain it concretely, for example "zustand actions declared as arrow properties are not symbols").

input.description: Build React twin of helpdesk
input.prompt:
Build a React twin of a Vue test-corpus app so we can measure, construct by construct, how much more of the code graph `entire graph` (a Go code-graph provider) extracts from React than from Vue.

## Inputs (read them first)
- Vue app: `/Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/helpdesk/`: Vue 2.7-style Options API, plain JavaScript, Vuex namespaced modules, mixins, `extends`, an event bus, global registration, jest specs. Its `expected.json` is a hand-written ground truth of ~316 facts (symbols, relations, absent traps), each tagged with a gap category. The README one level up explains the format and tags.
- Comparison tool: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/be8c9437-53d5-4e9f-bb9b-0907a051322f/scratchpad/tools/compare_twins.py`. Read its docstring. It maps every Vue fact to your twin through `twin-map.json` and scores both snapshots. Do not edit it; report problems instead.

## Build the twin at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-abhi-Documents-entire-graph/be8c9437-53d5-4e9f-bb9b-0907a051322f/scratchpad/twins/helpdesk-react/`
Only write inside that folder (the scratchpad is shared with other agents).

This is the legacy dialect twin: React class components in plain JavaScript `.jsx`, Redux, react-router. Mirror the Vue app file for file: every `src/**/X.vue` becomes `src/**/X.jsx` with the same component name; plain `.js` modules (api, utils, event bus) keep their paths and stay as close to verbatim as React allows; keep `jsconfig.json` with the `@/*` path alias, a bundler alias config, `package.json` (react, react-dom, react-redux, redux, redux-thunk, react-router-dom, jest, @testing-library/react or enzyme), `public/index.html`. Keep every component, method, action, mutation, helper and handler NAME identical to the Vue app, and keep the same call structure, so each Vue fact has an obvious React counterpart. The goal is that only the framework differs, not the code shape:
- Options API component -> `class X extends React.Component`. `methods` -> class methods with the same names; methods call each other via `this.other()` exactly as in Vue. `computed` -> class getters (`get openCount()`) with the same names. `watch` handlers -> methods with the same names invoked from `componentDidUpdate`. `created`/`mounted` -> `componentDidMount`; `beforeDestroy` -> `componentWillUnmount` (record these in `names`). `data()` -> `this.state` in the constructor.
- Template child tags (kebab-case `<ticket-row>`) and `@click="assign"` / `v-on:submit.prevent="fn"` -> JSX `<TicketRow>` and `onClick={this.assign}` with the same handler names.
- `this.$emit('reply-sent', reply)` -> `this.props.onReplySent(reply)`, and the parent passes `onReplySent={this.onReplySent}`.
- Mixins -> class inheritance or a base class chain that keeps the same member names (for example `class TicketList extends PaginatedComponent` where the base holds `nextPage`), so `this.nextPage()` still targets the shared member; map the mixin object symbol name to the base class name in `names`. `extends: BaseListView` -> `class X extends BaseListView`.
- Vuex namespaced modules -> Redux modules at the same paths: thunks and action creators with the same names as the Vuex actions (`fetchTickets = (params) => async (dispatch) => {...}`), reducer handling for each mutation kept as same-named functions (`SET_TICKETS(state, payload)`) inside an object the reducer dispatches to, and the same getter names as selector functions. Components call them the way Vuex code does: `this.props.dispatch(fetchTickets(...))` for `$store.dispatch`, and `connect(mapState, { fetchTickets })` + `this.props.fetchTickets()` for `mapActions`.
- The event bus stays an event emitter with the same channel names and `$emit`/`$on`/`$off` replaced by `emit`/`on`/`off` (for example a tiny emitter or `mitt`), used in the same functions.
- Global registration (`Vue.component('base-button', BaseButton)`) -> explicit imports in each user; same component names.
- vue-router -> react-router-dom with `lazy(() => import('@/views/TicketDetail'))` routes and the same `authGuard` function.
- `<script src="./TicketTimer.js">` and the pug template have no React equivalent: inline the logic and mark those facts no-counterpart.
- jest specs -> the same spec files and targets.

## twin-map.json (in the twin root)
`{"vue_ext": ".jsx", "files": {...}, "names": {...}, "no_counterpart": {...}}`. List every fact key that has no React counterpart in `no_counterpart` with a one-line reason; get the keys with `python3 -I .../tools/compare_twins.py --keys /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/helpdesk`. Keep `no_counterpart` honest and minimal: a construct that exists in React with different syntax is NOT no-counterpart (rendering `<ticket-row>` is a render in JSX too; a Vuex action call is a thunk call). Expected no-counterpart facts include component custom-event EMITS/LISTENS_ON edges (React uses callback props, not channels), HTML-id traps (`false-elements`), `document` symbols, `script-src`, and Vuex string-dispatch facts only where Redux has no named target. Use `names` only when React forces a different name, and `files` only for paths other than the default `.vue` -> `.jsx` swap.

## Validate
1. Snapshot: `.../scratchpad/corpus-check/entire-graph snapshot --repo <twin dir> --worktree --format ndjson > .../scratchpad/twins/helpdesk-react.ndjson`
2. Compare: `python3 -I .../tools/compare_twins.py /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph/internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/helpdesk .../scratchpad/corpus-check/helpdesk.ndjson .../scratchpad/twins/helpdesk-react .../scratchpad/twins/helpdesk-react.ndjson --details .../scratchpad/twins/helpdesk-details.json`
3. Fix until the tool reports zero MAPPING ERRORS. Do not change the twin's code to chase a better React score; mirror the Vue shapes faithfully and let the numbers fall where they fall.

## Final report (under 350 words)
The comparison table as printed, the no_counterpart count by tag with the main reasons, and the most important observations: for each tag where React scores well and Vue scores zero, what React edge exists; for tags where React also scores low, what the shared failure is (inspect `helpdesk-details.json` and the React snapshot to explain it concretely, for example "class getters are not emitted as symbols").

Map where in the `entire graph` provider (Go repo at /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph, logic under `internal/sem/`) each Vue-support improvement would land. I will turn your map into an ordered implementation plan, so I need precise `file:line` locations, the function names, and a short description of the current logic. Do not propose full code. Thoroughness: very thorough, but report concisely.

With both twins in, I can estimate the main fix before anyone writes Go. I'll extract each `.vue` file's script blocks into a plain `.ts`/`.js` file. The template is blanked to spaces, so every line number stays the same, and `.vue` import specifiers are rewritten. Then I score that with the same tool. """Approximate "parse .vue script blocks as JS/TS" without touching the provider.

usage: python3 -I simulate_sfc.py VUE_APP_DIR OUT_DIR

Copies the app. Each X.vue becomes X.ts / X.tsx / X.js holding only its
<script> and <script setup> bodies; every other byte is blanked to a space and
newlines are kept, so line numbers match the .vue file. Import specifiers that
end in .vue lose the extension so extensionless resolution finds the new file.
Writes OUT_DIR/twin-map.json mapping each .vue path to its simulated file.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

SCRIPT = re.compile(r"<script\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</script>", re.S)
LANG = re.compile(r"""\blang\s*=\s*["']([a-z]+)["']""")
VUE_SPEC = re.compile(r"""(['"])([^'"\n]+?)\.vue\1""")


def extract(source):
    keep = [False] * len(source)
    langs = set()
    for match in SCRIPT.finditer(source):
        lang = LANG.search(match.group(1))
        langs.add(lang.group(1) if lang else "js")
        for i in range(match.start(2), match.end(2)):
            keep[i] = True
    out = "".join(ch if keep[i] or ch == "\n" else " " for i, ch in enumerate(source))
    ext = ".tsx" if "tsx" in langs else ".ts" if "ts" in langs else ".js"
    return out, ext


def main(src, dst):
    if os.path.exists(dst):
        shutil.rmtree(dst)
    shutil.copytree(src, dst)
    files = {}
    for root, _, names in os.walk(dst):
        for name in names:
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, dst)
            if name.endswith(".vue"):
                body, ext = extract(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
                body = VUE_SPEC.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2) + m.group(1), body)
                os.remove(path)
                target = path[:-4] + ext
                open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(body)
                files[rel] = rel[:-4] + ext
            elif name.endswith((".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx")):
                text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
                rewritten = VUE_SPEC.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2) + m.group(1), text)
                if rewritten != text:
                    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(rewritten)
    json.dump({"vue_ext": ".ts", "files": files}, open(os.path.join(dst, "twin-map.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    print(f"{len(files)} .vue files converted")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

entire graph · branch vue-corpus · identity revision 8 · 2026-11-18

Vue Support Roadmap

We ran Graph on two Vue apps and on React twins of both. The twins have the same files, names, and call paths in idiomatic React. On the 568 facts that have a React counterpart, Graph finds 384 in React and 205 in Vue. Parsing the <script> blocks as JavaScript would recover 142 facts with no other change. The remaining work splits into Vue semantics, JavaScript resolution bugs that React shares, and template edges that neither framework gets today.

206 / 622facts in the Vue graph today
384 / 568comparable facts in the React twins
348 / 622Vue after Step 2, simulated
151missing facts React also misses

How We Measured

  • React twins. taskboard-react uses TSX function components, zustand stores shaped like the Pinia stores, and react-router. helpdesk-react uses JSX class components, Redux thunks named after the Vuex actions, class inheritance in place of mixins, and the same event bus. A twin-map.json maps every Vue fact to its React counterpart. 54 facts have no counterpart: custom-event channels, attribute traps, and <script src>.
  • Simulation. Each .vue file was rewritten as a .ts/.js file holding only its script bodies, with the template blanked to spaces so line numbers match. That approximates Step 2 without writing Go.
  • Limits. Step gains below come from assigning each missing fact to the first step that the twin and simulation evidence say it needs, so read them as upper bounds. Twin matching ignores symbol kind, which let one interface field pass as a store getter.

Steps

Steps 0 to 2 are sequential. Steps 3 to 5 are independent and can run in parallel. Step 5 also lifts React and every plain JavaScript or TypeScript repo. Each step ends with go test ./internal/sem -run TestVueCorpusScore -update to record its gain.

Step 0

Lock In the Measurement

0 facts
  • Commit the corpus on vue-corpus: vue_corpus_test.go, both apps, score.json.
  • Add the React twins as testdata/vuecorpus/react/{taskboard,helpdesk} with their twin-map.json. Port the comparison script into vue_corpus_test.go so the score log prints a React parity column per tag. Every later PR then shows Vue against its parity target.
Step 1

Stop Silent False Negatives

0 facts, ships first
  • In the impact and neighbors renderers, when inventory-only files in a script-bearing language mention the symbol name, print a line such as “4 Vue files mention useCart but are not parsed”, and count those files in the coverage footer.
  • This stops today's confident “0 callers” answers. It stays useful for Svelte and other inventory-only languages after Vue is parsed.
Step 2

Parse Script Blocks as JavaScript or TypeScript

+142 facts · 206 → 348
  • Masked view. Add internal/sem/vue.go modeled on flowjs.go. It blanks every byte outside the <script> and <script setup> bodies, keeping byte length and newlines (the maskLineText contract, parser.go:3711). It picks the grammar and TS mask from lang=: ts, tsx, or JavaScript.
  • Parse. In ParseWithStatusCtx (parser.go:423), branch before the no-grammar fallback (:483). Use the masked view as both parseSrc and entitySrc, walk with the dialect name so TS-only branches apply, append componentEntities, and return the label Vue. Script symbols get IDs like repo:Vue:path:function:name, and existing component IDs stay unchanged.
  • Relation phase. Apply the same mask where relations reread the file (provider.go:5530, before importsFor) and in jsScanGrammar (js_scopes.go:118). Every reader must see identical bytes.
  • Gates. Add isJavaScriptFamily(language) and use it in callExtractionLanguage (provider.go:1017), channelScanLanguage (:1938), the route, HTTP, and service gates (:1911, :1920, :1929), types.go:86 and :2344, the language group in langcompat.go:58, and flowSyntaxFor (flow_syntax.go:35), where Vue falls through to Python patterns today. Carry the dialect per file for the TS-only tiers (typescript.go:83, provider.go:5692, receiverCallRelations).
  • Resolution. Add .vue to jsLocalImportCandidates (provider.go:20949), to jsModuleFiles (:21337) and resolveJSModulePath (:22693) through a new jsModuleExtension helper, and to importScanners (:23698) and importedNamesFor. Do not widen jsLikeExtension, which also feeds the Express and NestJS passes.
  • Capabilities. Special-case Vue in supportsSemanticExtraction (provider.go:882) as SQL and Groovy are, so the fast profile runs. Add a Vue entry to ooRelationSupport, then update docs/language-support.md, language_matrix_test.go, and the capability-union probe.
  • Recovers: script-symbols 37, options-api 41, script-imports 18, script-calls 18, path-alias 16, ts-types 7, lazy-imports 5.

Risks: one reader that sees raw bytes misattributes template text, and any byte drift corrupts every offset. The whole-file component symbol is not type-like (types.go:12), so it would be scanned as a caller of everything. Exclude it from call scanning. Bump IdentityRevision (provider.go:89), whose value feeds both cache prefixes, and regenerate the goldens.

Step 3

Give the Component Its Script

+27 facts
  • Containment and callers. Make the component the container of its top-level script symbols and the caller for top-level <script setup> statements, matching React's function component. lexicalEntityParents (nested_containers.go:67) already makes the whole-file component the parent once scripts parse. Verify the CONTAINS edges and attribute top-level calls to the component rather than the file.
  • Prop types. Emit USES_TYPE from the component for defineProps<Props>(), withDefaults, and defineEmits<T>().
  • Options API container. Give export default {…} and defineComponent({…}) a container entity in javascriptDefaultExportEntities (parser.go:8829), so this.x() resolves (provider.go:8152). Plain JavaScript benefits too.
  • Recovers: component-owner 12, options-api 10, ts-types 5.
Step 4

Vue Runtime Patterns

+24 facts, plus custom events
  • Events. Change emitCallRe and listenCallRe (types.go:327) to accept $emit, $on, $once, and $off, and drop dispatch from the emit verbs. That also removes the false EMITS for dispatch('auth/restoreSession'). Emit EMITS for emit('x') from defineEmits and for this.$emit('x').
  • Mixins. Turn mixins: [m] into INHERITS and extends: Base into EXTENDS from the component, and resolve this.x() into mixin and base members. React gets all 15 of these through class inheritance.
  • Vuex strings. Map dispatch('ns/action'), commit('ns/M'), and mapActions/mapGetters to heuristic CALLS on the module member, resolving the namespace through the modules map in the store root.
  • Recovers: mixins 15, event-bus 9, plus the EMITS half of the 27 custom-event facts.
Step 5

Fix the Shared JavaScript Engine Gaps

+103 facts, React too

Independent PRs, each with its own fixture:

  • Stores and hooks (store-members 29, component-owner 7):
    • Accept export const useX = defineStore(…) and create(…) as call targets in callableTargetKind (provider.go:2418).
    • Stop treating @/ modules as external in importedExternalSymbolName (:10526).
    • Resolve member calls through returned and destructured objects (factoryReturnVarTypes at types.go:3157, nameCallMayTargetMethod at provider.go:2475).
  • Arrow properties as symbols (store getters 12). Add a pair case to entityFromNode (parser.go:6065) using functionLikeValue.
  • Calls and imports (js-resolution 7, plus scattered script facts):
    • Allow nested sibling calls in localReachable (provider.go:2439).
    • Scan multi-line imports in scanJSImports (:23854).
    • Keep the imported name for a as b (importedJavaScriptNames, :24065).
    • Skip same-name callees at :6002, :6048, :6189, and :6262 only when the name has no import binding.
    • Strip /* webpackChunkName */ before reading the specifier (:23852, :23876).
  • Config (path-alias 9, lazy-imports 9). Read jsconfig.json, follow tsconfig references such as tsconfig.app.json, and strip block comments and trailing commas (stripJSONLineComments, :22392; manifestImportFiles, :21193).
  • False positives (false-relations 6):
    • Treat name(params) { as a declaration in jsOpenParenStartsDeclarationOrControl (call_scanners.go:117).
    • Stop bare get( and post( on a local HTTP wrapper from matching routingCallRe (provider.go:25386, :25391).
  • Tests (tests 17). Emit TESTS from vitest and jest describe/it/test blocks to the imported subject (testRelations, provider.go:12773). Today TESTS comes only from name conventions in testSubjectName (types.go:280).

Risk: these change caller counts in every JavaScript and TypeScript repo and move the typescript-* goldens. Bump the cache prefixes and regenerate goldens and quality_coverage.json in the same PR.

Step 6

Template and JSX Edges

+63 facts, React too
  • Template walker. Walk the Vue template block. Resolve PascalCase and kebab-case tags through the script's import bindings (resolveImportSpecPath, provider.go:24187) or a global registry built from app.component/Vue.component. Map @event and v-on handler names to CALLS on script functions, and @custom-event to LISTENS_ON.
  • JSX. Add the same walker for JSX elements and attributes. No JSX node is referenced anywhere today, so React gains the same 63 facts.
  • Relation type. Decide between existing heuristic CALLS/ACCESSES and a new additive RENDERS type. A new type touches relationTypes (provider.go:103), the capability matrix, and the additive-only rule in ADR 0001.
  • Recovers: template-edges 49, global-registration 14, plus the LISTENS_ON half of the custom-event facts.
Step 7

Vue-Only Remainders

+30 facts
  • HTML ids. Fix htmlEntitiesIdRe to require whitespace or a tag start before id=, and skip bound :id and v-bind:id. That clears 20 traps such as :data-task-id="task.id" becoming an element named id. Pair it with the Step 2 revision bump.
  • External scripts. Treat <script src="./x.js"> as an IMPORTS edge, and treat the target file as the component's script (script-src 7).

content.text:
The comparison is done, and the steps to improve Vue support are published: **https://claude.ai/artifact/VQ98xJbyaCgNTzQTRUNE9a** (private until you share it).

I built a React twin of each Vue app with the same files, names, and call paths, written as normal React. Then I ran Graph on all four:

| | Facts found |
|---|---|
| Vue today | **206 / 622** (33%) |
| Vue, on the 568 facts that have a React equivalent | 205 / 568 |
| React twins, same 568 facts | **384 / 568** (68%) |
| Vue with script blocks parsed (simulated) | 348 / 622 (56%) |

The simulation rewrote each `.vue` file as a plain `.ts`/`.js` file holding only its script, with the same line numbers. It estimates the main fix without writing any Go.

**Where the 416 missing Vue facts come from:**
- **142: script blocks are never parsed.** Parsing them alone recovers these.
- **51: Vue-specific behavior the engine doesn't model.** React gets the equivalent today through syntax the engine already handles: a component function containing its handlers, class `extends`, typed parameters, `.emit`.
- **103: JavaScript bugs React has too.** Store and hook member calls, arrow-function getters, nested sibling calls, multi-line and aliased imports, `jsconfig.json` aliases, vitest/jest TESTS edges, and three false-positive patterns.
- **63: no template or JSX edges in either framework.** Nothing links `<TaskCard>` or `onClick={fn}` to the code they use.
- **57: Vue-only constructs.** Custom-event channels, HTML-id traps, `<script src>`.

**The steps, each with its measured gain and the exact provider functions to change:**

| Step | What | Gain | Vue after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Commit the corpus and the React twins; print a React comparison column per gap in the score test | 0 | 206 |
| 1 | Warn in `impact`/`neighbors` when unparsed Vue files mention the symbol, instead of a confident "0 callers" | 0 | 206 |
| 2 | Parse `<script>` blocks with the JS/TS grammar; treat Vue as JavaScript in ~40 language checks; resolve `.vue` imports | +142 | 348 |
| 3 | Make each component own its script: containment, setup calls, `defineProps` types, `this` in Options API | +27 | 375 |
| 4 | `$emit`/`$on`, mixins, Vuex `dispatch`/`commit` strings | +37 | 412 |
| 5 | JavaScript bug fixes (React improves too) | +103 | 515 |
| 6 | Template and JSX edges for rendered components and event handlers | +77 | 592 |
| 7 | HTML-id regex, `<script src>` | +30 | 622 |

Steps 3 to 5 are independent and can run in parallel. Step 2's risks are on the page: every part of the provider that rereads a file must see the identical masked bytes, and the whole-file component symbol must be excluded from call scanning.

Read the gains as upper bounds. Each missing fact is assigned to the first step the twin and simulation evidence point to. Only Step 2's number is directly measured.

The React twins and the two comparison scripts are in this session's scratchpad, which may be cleared. Shall I move them into the repo as Step 0? The `vue-corpus` branch itself is still uncommitted.

Design an implementation plan for better Vue single-file-component support in `entire graph`, a Go code-graph provider at /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph (logic in `internal/sem/`). Read AGENTS.md first for the contract rules: frozen additive-only schema 1.x (docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md), no-egress, stable `compound-v1` symbol IDs, `IdentityRevision` bump (provider.go:~89) when parser output re-keys symbols, partial failures never silent. Use `entire graph query/def/neighbors/impact --repo . --head` to locate code, then read focused source.

## Evidence already gathered (do not redo)
- `.vue` files are inventory-only today: `languageForPath` maps `.vue` to language "Vue" with no grammar (parser.go:~132), `ParseWithStatusCtx` (parser.go:423) sends grammar-less specs to `fallbackEntities` (~483) -> `componentEntities` (~4128): a whole-file `component` symbol plus HTML-id `element` symbols (`htmlEntitiesIdRe`, which wrongly matches `:task-id=`/`data-id=`).
- A scored corpus exists on branch `vue-corpus` (uncommitted): `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/{taskboard,helpdesk}` with `expected.json` ground truth (622 tagged facts), `internal/sem/vue_corpus_test.go` (`TestVueCorpusManifestMatchesSource`, `TestVueCorpusScore` ratcheting `score.json`, `-update` flag, `VUE_CORPUS_VERBOSE=1`). Vue scores 206/622 today. React twins of both apps (same names and call paths) score 384/568 comparable facts. A simulation that rewrote each .vue as a .ts/.js file holding only its script bodies (template blanked, newlines kept) scored 348/622.
- Missing facts by cause: 142 fixed by parsing scripts; 51 need Vue semantics (component containment and top-level setup calls attributed to the component, `defineProps<Props>()` USES_TYPE, Options API `export default {}` container so `this.x()` resolves, mixins -> INHERITS and `this` into mixin members, `$emit`/`$on` events, Vuex `dispatch('ns/a')`/`commit` strings); 103 shared JS/TS engine gaps also failing in React (store/hook member calls through returned or destructured objects; const-bound factories like `export const useX = defineStore(...)` rejected by `callableTargetKind` provider.go:~2418 and `@/` imports turned external in `importedExternalSymbolName` ~10526; arrow-function object properties not symbols, no `pair` case in `entityFromNode` parser.go:~6065; nested sibling calls blocked by `localReachable` ~2439; multi-line imports in `scanJSImports` ~23854; aliased imports `importedJavaScriptNames` ~24065; same-name callee skip `if name == from.Name { continue }` at ~6002/6048/6189/6262; `webpackChunkName` comment ~23852/23876; jsconfig.json and tsconfig `references` not read, `stripJSONLineComments` ~22392; false CALLS to `state` from `jsOpenParenStartsDeclarationOrControl` call_scanners.go:~117; false EMITS because `emitCallRe` types.go:327 includes `dispatch`; false HANDLES_ROUTE for bare `get(`/`post(` `routingCallRe` ~25386/25391; no vitest/jest TESTS, `testRelations` ~12773); 63 template/JSX edges missing in both (no JSX node handling anywhere); 57 Vue-only constructs.

## Proposed core design for parsing (validate or refute against the code)
1. `internal/sem/vue.go` (modeled on `flowjs.go`): `vueScriptView(content) (masked string, dialect string, hasScript bool)` blanks every byte outside top-level `<script>` and `<script setup>` bodies, keeping byte length and newlines (the `maskLineText` contract, parser.go:~3711); dialect from `lang=`: ts -> TypeScript grammar + TS mask, tsx -> TSX grammar + TSX mask, otherwise JavaScript.
2. Parse phase: refactor the body of `ParseWithStatusCtx` after spec selection into a helper taking (spec, a tsx/flow variant flag instead of `filepath.Ext(path)` checks at ~559-565, content) so the Vue branch can parse the masked view under the dialect spec (so every `spec.language == "TypeScript"/"JavaScript"` branch, including the supplemental passes at ~657, applies), then append `componentEntities` on the original content and return the label "Vue". IDs become `repo:Vue:path:function:name`; existing component/element IDs unchanged. No script -> today's behavior.
3. Relation phase, two seams instead of ~40 gate edits: (a) wrap `readContent` at the top of `forEachRelation` (provider.go:5012; callers at ~1694 and `buildRelations` ~4795) so every reread of a `.vue` path returns the masked view; (b) compute a per-file analysis language once (dialect for Vue files) and use it wherever the per-file worker reads `file.Language` (~5528-6900), plus a small helper for the ~7 symbol-level checks (`symbol.Language`/`from.Language` at ~4548, ~4617, ~7875, ~8002, ~8273, ~8321, ~8346) and `langcompat.go:58` cross-language groups. Keep the emitted file and symbol language "Vue".
4. Resolution: `.vue` in `jsLocalImportCandidates` (~20949), `jsModuleFiles` (~21337) and `resolveJSModulePath` (~22693) via a new `jsModuleExtension` helper (do not widen `jsLikeExtension`, which feeds Express/NestJS passes), `importScanners` (~23698) and `importedNamesFor`.
5. Capabilities: `supportsSemanticExtraction` (~882) special-case Vue like SQL/Groovy; `ooRelationSupport`; docs/language-support.md; `language_matrix_test.go`; capability-union probe; goldens and `quality_coverage.json`; `IdentityRevision` and cache prefixes.
Known risks to check: the whole-file `component` symbol is not `typeLikeKind` (types.go:12) so it would be scanned as a caller of everything; `lexicalEntityParents` (nested_containers.go:67) will make it the container of every script symbol (good for CONTAINS, check for side effects in search container maps); the fast profile `skipFastProfilePerSymbolScan`; `js_scopes.go:118` `jsScanGrammar` picks a grammar by extension; any other reader of raw content in the relation phase not going through `readContent`; where symbol `Language` is assigned from `parsedLanguage` (provider_parallel.go:~302/306, `entitySymbols`).

## What I need back
1. Confirm or correct the core design, with file:line evidence for anything that breaks it (especially: other raw-content readers, places that derive grammar or language from the file extension during relations, search/ranking code that would mis-handle Vue script symbols).
2. A PR-by-PR breakdown of the whole roadmap (steps: 0 corpus+React twins+parity column in the test; 1 impact/neighbors warning when inventory-only files mention the symbol; 2 script parsing; 3 component semantics; 4 Vue runtime patterns; 5 shared JS engine fixes split into independent PRs; 6 template and JSX edges; 7 HTML-id regex and `<script src>`), each PR with: files and functions to change, existing helpers to reuse, tests to add (unit fixture + expected corpus tags), cache/golden obligations, and the risk. Keep each PR reviewable (<~800 lines of non-test change).
3. For Step 6, recommend whether template/JSX render and handler edges should reuse existing relation types (CALLS/ACCESSES with heuristic resolution) or add an additive RENDERS type, citing what a new type touches (`relationTypes` ~103, capability matrix tests, ADR 0001).
Keep the response under ~1800 words.

questions.question: How far should this implementation plan go? (The roadmap has 8 steps, numbered 0 to 7, from 206/622 facts today to an estimated ~600.)

options.label: Full roadmap, PR by PR (Recommended)
options.description: Plan all steps (0 to 7) as a sequence of reviewable PRs, with Steps 0 to 2 in full detail and later PRs at file and function level.

options.label: First milestone only
options.description: Plan Steps 0 to 2 in depth (corpus, impact warning, script parsing): 206 to ~348 facts. Later steps are listed only.

options.label: Vue-specific only
options.description: Plan Steps 0 to 4 and 7. Skip the shared JS engine fixes (Step 5) and template/JSX edges (Step 6), which also change React and plain JS output.

questions.question: Template edges (`<TaskCard>` rendered by BoardView, `@click="toggle"`) need a relation type, and the same choice will apply to JSX. Which should the plan use?

options.label: Reuse CALLS/ACCESSES (Recommended)
options.description: Mark them as heuristic resolution with template evidence. No schema change, and existing impact/neighbors queries see them at once.

options.label: Add a RENDERS type
options.description: A clearer meaning, but it is an additive schema change: relationTypes, the capability matrix, docs, and the ADR 0001 process. Callers must also opt in to the new type.

options.label: Decide later
options.description: Leave Step 6 at outline level and decide when the earlier steps have landed.

questions.question: Should Step 5's shared JavaScript fixes (store/hook member calls, arrow getters, nested calls, imports, jsconfig, vitest/jest TESTS, false positives) be planned as part of the Vue effort?

options.label: Yes, as separate PRs (Recommended)
options.description: Each fix is its own PR with a plain JS/TS fixture. Each also lifts React and every JS repo, and moves the typescript-* goldens.

options.label: Only Vue-blocking ones
options.description: Include only fixes that most Vue facts depend on (store calls, arrow getters, jsconfig alias). Leave the rest for the JS backlog.

options.label: No, track separately
options.description: Keep the Vue plan to Vue-specific changes and file the JS fixes as separate issues.

# Plan: Better Vue Support in entire graph (Vue-Specific Scope)

## Context

`.vue` files are inventory-only today. `languageForPath` maps `.vue` to language `Vue` with no grammar. `ParseWithStatusCtx` (`internal/sem/parser.go:423`) sends it to `fallbackEntities` and then `componentEntities`. That emits one whole-file `component` symbol plus HTML-id `element` symbols, and never parses `<script>`. Agents asking `impact`/`neighbors` about code used by Vue components get a confident "0 callers".

We measured this on branch `vue-corpus` (uncommitted):

- **Corpus.** `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/{taskboard,helpdesk}` has 622 tagged ground-truth facts, scored by `internal/sem/vue_corpus_test.go` and ratcheted in `score.json`. Vue scores **206/622**.
- **React twins.** Apps with the same names and call paths score **384/568** comparable facts.
- **Simulation.** Parsing only the script bodies scores **348/622**.

Scope decided with the user:

- **In:** Vue-specific Steps 0 to 4 and 7.
- **Tracked separately:** the shared JS/TS engine fixes (Step 5).
- **Deferred:** template/JSX edges (Step 6). The relation type is still undecided.

Target: **206 → ~442/622 (71%)**, with each PR recording its gain in `score.json`.

## Ground Rules (AGENTS.md)

- **Schema** 1.x is frozen and additive-only. The provider is no-egress.
- **IDs.** Existing `compound-v1` IDs stay stable: the `component`/`document`/`element` IDs of `.vue` files must not change.
- **Cache revision.** Any change to parser output bumps `IdentityRevision` (`provider.go:89`, changelog comment above it) in the same commit, because the record and search caches key on the git tree.
- **Failures.** A script that fails to parse surfaces as a partial failure with `Language: "Vue"`. No silent drops.
- **Each PR ends with:**
  - `go test ./internal/sem -run TestVueCorpus -update` (records the gain)
  - `go test ./internal/sem -run TestProviderGoldenSnapshots -update` when goldens move
  - `mise run check`

## Core Design: Parse Under the Dialect, Report as Vue

Copy the Flow JS precedent (`parser.go:441`, `flowjs.go`): swap the grammar, keep the label. A Vue file is analyzed as its script dialect (`TypeScript` or `JavaScript`) everywhere internally, and emitted as `Vue`. Two seams then replace ~40 scattered language checks:

1. **Parse seam.** The Vue branch parses a masked script view under the dialect spec. Every existing `spec.language == "TypeScript"/"JavaScript"` branch runs unchanged, including the masks at `parser.go:559-565` and the supplemental passes at `parser.go:657-661`. The branch then appends `componentEntities` and returns the label `Vue`. Script symbol IDs become `repo:Vue:path:function:name`.
2. **Relation seam.** At the top of `forEachRelation` (`provider.go:5012`), wrap `readContent` so every reread of a `.vue` path returns the masked view. Compute a per-file analysis language (the dialect) once and use it where the per-file worker reads `file.Language` (`provider.go:5528-6900`). The ~7 symbol-level checks (`provider.go:4548`, `4617`, `7875`, `8002`, `8273`, `8321`, `8346`) and `langcompat.go:58` go through a small `analysisLanguage` helper.

(PLAN AGENT REVIEW PENDING: PR boundaries and risk notes below are refined from it.)

# Plan: Semantic support for Vue single-file components

## Context

There is no existing Vue plan. Nothing in `docs/`, Linear, or Brain covers it; the only mention is a
"Priority 2: HTML/CSS, Vue, Svelte" line in `docs/archive/2026-06-18-entire-graph-v2-implementation-plan.md:561`.

Today `.vue` is recognized (`internal/sem/parser.go:129`, no grammar) and routed to
`componentEntities` (`parser.go:3569`, `:3802`). That function emits one `component` entity for the file
and one `element` entity per HTML `id=` (via `htmlEntities`, `parser.go:3767`). The `<script>` block is
never parsed. As a result, Vue repos produce no functions, calls, imports, or types, so `query`,
`neighbors`, and `impact` give nothing useful for Vue code. Vue is also missing from the semantic
language list in `docs/language-support.md`.

Goal: parse the `<script>` / `<script setup>` blocks with the existing JS/TS tree-sitter pipeline. Vue
then gets the same symbols and relations as `.ts`/`.js` files, existing Vue symbol IDs stay stable, and
the no-egress and frozen-schema rules hold (no new grammar download, no schema break).

## Approach: mask the SFC and reuse the JS/TS grammar

The repo already parses many languages by masking the source first (`maskTypeScriptUnsupportedSyntax`,
`maskTSXUnsupportedSyntax`, `maskFlowJavaScriptUnsupportedSyntax` in `parser.go:336-347`). Each mask
blanks bytes but keeps byte offsets and line numbers. Vue fits the same pattern:

1. **`maskVueSFC(content) (masked string, grammarExt string)`** (new file `internal/sem/vue.go`)
   - Find the top-level `<script …>` and `<script setup …>` blocks.
   - Keep their inner text. Replace every other non-newline byte with a space, so lines and columns map
     1:1 and no range remapping is needed.
   - Pick the grammar from `lang=`: `ts` → TypeScript, `tsx` → TSX, otherwise (none, `js`, `jsx`)
     → JavaScript. When the two blocks use different languages, use TS.
   - Then run the TS mask on the result too, so TS-only syntax gets the same treatment as in `.ts`
     files.

2. **Grammar routing in `TreeSitterParser.ParseWithStatus`** (`parser.go:242`)
   - For `spec.language == "Vue"`, mask the source, choose the grammar from step 1, and run the normal
     `walkEntities` path, plus the JS extras at `parser.go:402-404`
     (`javascriptExportedVariableEntities`, `javascriptAssignmentMethodEntities`).
   - Keep the reported language as `"Vue"` for file records and capabilities.
   - **Keep the existing entities** from `componentEntities` (the file component and HTML ids)
     unchanged and append the script entities, so their `compound-v1` IDs do not change.
   - If there is no `<script>` block, keep today's behavior. That is not a failure.

3. **Treat Vue as JS-family wherever logic keys on language or extension**
   - Add `isJavaScriptFamily(language string) bool` (JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue). Then go through the
     roughly 36 `"TypeScript"`/`"JavaScript"` checks in `parser.go` and `provider.go` and switch only the
     ones that are about script semantics: calls, data flow, types, and exported variables.
   - In the extension-keyed switches in `provider.go` (`:20379`, `:20397`, `:20432`, `:22191`), add
     `.vue`. Register `.vue` in `importScanners` (`provider.go:23172`) with `jsImportFn` applied to the
     **masked** content, so imports in the template or comments are not picked up.
   - Module resolution: make `import Foo from './Foo.vue'` resolve to that file's component symbol, in
     both `.vue` and `.ts`/`.js` importers. Also add `.vue` to the extensionless-resolution candidate
     list.

4. **Vue-specific symbols (phase 2, same PR if small)**
   - Options API: create `method` entities for the members of `methods`, `computed`, and `watch` inside
     `export default {…}` / `defineComponent({…})`, contained by the file's component entity.
   - Template → script relations: tags that match imported component identifiers (PascalCase or
     kebab-case) and `@event="handler"` / `v-on` handlers that name a script function. Emit these with
     an **existing** relation type (e.g. `CALLS` or a reference type, resolution `heuristic`). The 1.x
     schema is additive-only, so do not add a new type unless it is truly needed (ADR 0001).

5. **Cache identity**
   - The parser output for `.vue` changes while git trees stay the same, so bump `IdentityRevision`
     (`provider.go:63`, `"4"` → `"5"`) in the same commit. Without the bump, cached snapshots keep
     serving Vue files with no script symbols (see AGENTS.md).

6. **Failures and coverage**
   - A parse error inside the script block → `E_PARSE_ERROR` partial failure with `Language: "Vue"`.
     Do not drop it silently.
   - Move Vue to `semantic_languages` in `capabilities`. Regenerate `docs/language-support.md`
     (36 → 37 semantic languages).

**Out of scope (follow-up):** Svelte uses the same `componentEntities` path and could reuse `maskVueSFC`
almost unchanged, but its `$:` reactive statements and `{#each}` template logic need their own design.
Also out of scope: `<style>` blocks (CSS entities) and `lang="coffee"`/pug templates. Unsupported
`lang` values keep today's behavior and get a warning diagnostic.

## Critical files

- `internal/sem/vue.go` (new): mask, block scanner, options-API and template helpers
- `internal/sem/parser.go`: `.vue` spec (`:129`), `ParseWithStatus` (`:242`), `fallbackEntities`
  switch (`:3569`), `componentEntities` (`:3802`)
- `internal/sem/provider.go`: JS-family branches, `importScanners` (`:23172`), module resolution,
  `IdentityRevision` (`:63`)
- `internal/sem/inventory_languages.go` / capabilities: semantic tier
- `docs/language-support.md`
- Reuse: `jsImportFn`, `walkEntities`, `maskTypeScriptUnsupportedSyntax`, `appendMissingEntities`,
  `simpleFallbackEntity`

## Verification

- New fixtures under `internal/sem/testdata/fixtures/vue/`: options API (JS), `<script setup lang="ts">`,
  both blocks, `lang="tsx"`, no script, broken script.
- Table tests (`internal/sem/vue_test.go`):
  - entities have the right names, kinds, and **original line numbers**
  - imports come from the script only
  - a `CALLS` edge from a setup function to an imported `.ts` function
  - a `.ts` importing `./Foo.vue` resolves
  - the broken script yields `E_PARSE_ERROR`
  - the existing `formats-config/component.vue` component and `vue-app` element IDs are unchanged
    (regression)
- Run `go test ./internal/sem -run 'Vue|Component'`, then `mise run check`.
- End to end: `mise run build`, then on a local Vue app checkout run `./entire-graph capabilities --json`
  (Vue is semantic), `./entire-graph query --repo <app> --query "<component behavior>"`, and
  `./entire-graph neighbors --repo <app> --symbol <setupFn> --direction in`. Confirm the results point at
  correct `file.vue:line` spans.

# Plan: Better Vue Support in entire graph (Vue-Specific Scope)

## Context

`.vue` files are inventory-only today. `languageForPath` maps `.vue` to `Vue` with no grammar. `ParseWithStatusCtx` (`internal/sem/parser.go:423`) sends it to `fallbackEntities` and then `componentEntities` (~4128). That emits one whole-file `component` symbol plus HTML-id `element` symbols, and never parses `<script>`. Agents asking `impact`/`neighbors` about code used by Vue components get a confident "0 callers".

Measured on branch `vue-corpus` (uncommitted):

- **Corpus.** `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/{taskboard,helpdesk}` holds 622 tagged ground-truth facts, scored by `vue_corpus_test.go` and ratcheted in `score.json`. Vue scores **206/622**.
- **React twins.** Apps with the same names and call paths score **384/568** comparable facts.
- **Simulation.** Parsing only the script bodies scores **348/622**.

Scope agreed with the user:

- **In:** Vue-specific Steps 0 to 4 and 7.
- **Tracked separately:** the shared JS/TS engine fixes (Step 5).
- **Deferred:** template/JSX edges (Step 6). The relation type is undecided.

Target: **206 → ~442/622 (71%)**. Every PR records its gain in `score.json`.

## Ground Rules (AGENTS.md)

- **Schema.** 1.x is frozen and additive-only, and the provider is no-egress.
- **IDs.** Existing `compound-v1` IDs stay stable. The `component`/`document`/`element` IDs of `.vue` files must not change.
- **Cache revision.** A parser output change bumps `IdentityRevision` (`provider.go:89`, changelog comment above it). A relation-only change bumps `providerRecordsCacheVersion` (`records_cache.go:57`) and `searchSnapshotCacheVersion` (`search_cache.go:64`).
- **Failures.** Unparseable scripts surface as partial failures with `Language: "Vue"`, never silent drops.
- **Every PR ends with:**
  - `go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus|TestProviderGolden|TestCapabilityMatrix|TestRelationFacts' -count=1`, plus `-update` where a baseline legitimately moves
  - `mise run check`

## Core Design: Parse Under the Dialect, Report as Vue

Follow the Flow JS precedent (`parser.go:441`, `flowjs.go`): swap the grammar, keep the label. Internally a Vue file is its script dialect (`TypeScript` or `JavaScript`). On the wire it stays `Vue`.

**Masked view.** New `internal/sem/vue.go` provides `vueScriptView(content)`. It keeps the bodies of top-level `<script>` and `<script setup>` and blanks every other byte to a space, keeping newlines (the `maskLineText` contract, `parser.go:3711`). It handles nested `<template>` tags, `<!-- -->` comments, CRLF line endings, and two script blocks. `vueScriptDialect` maps `lang=`:

| `lang=` | Grammar |
|---|---|
| `ts` | TypeScript |
| `tsx` | TSX |
| none, `js`, `jsx` | JavaScript |
| anything else (`coffee`) | none: today's fallback |

**Parse seam.**
- Extract the body of `ParseWithStatusCtx` after spec selection into a helper that takes `(spec, variant{tsx, flow}, content)`. The variant flags replace the `filepath.Ext` checks at ~431-438 and ~559-565.
- The Vue branch passes the masked view as `content`. Both `entitySrc` (walked at ~624) and the supplemental regex passes (~657-662) read it, so all of them see the masked view.
- Prepend `componentEntities(raw content)` and return `Vue`. Script symbols get IDs like `repo:Vue:path:function:name`, with no collisions (`entitySymbols`, `provider.go:2212`).
- Set containers explicitly: script symbols under the `component`, elements under the `document` as today. `lexicalEntityParents` (`nested_containers.go:67`) needs encloser-first order, and `component` and `document` share one range, so use a Vue-only sort (start ascending, end descending) and a test.

**Relation seam** (`forEachRelation`, `provider.go:5012`):
1. Wrap `readContent` so every reread of a `.vue` path returns the masked view. It is the only content reader in the phase that matters; the other readers in the phase (`collectRegistrationAliases`, `syntheticBoundarySymbols`) are harmless.
2. `resolveFileRelations` takes `file` by value (~5511), so shadow `file.Language = relationLanguage(file)` there. Vue becomes `TypeScript` for analysis.
3. Turn route, service, and channel scans off explicitly for Vue. Otherwise component `api.get(` calls would emit false HANDLES_ROUTE, and `dispatch(` false EMITS.
4. In `jsScanGrammar` (`js_scopes.go:118`), route `.vue` to the TypeScript-then-TSX fallback that `newJSScanStateForContent` (~95) already uses. No dialect plumbing is needed.
5. Two helpers cover the ~15 symbol-level checks: `jsFamilyLanguage` (JS, TS, or Vue) and `tsRulesLanguage` (TS or Vue). They apply at:
   - `provider.go:4548, 4617, 7875, 8002, 8273, 8321`
   - `types.go:2316` (`signatureTypeReferences`) and `supertypesFromSignature` (~5302, 7068)
   - `search_container_map.go:456`
   - `declaration_line.go:294`
   - `langcompat.go:58` (the JS/TS group)
6. Keep `provider.go:8346` literal. Its TypeScript fallback would resolve `ticket.save()` to the component's own `save`.
7. Keep `component` and `element` symbols out of the per-symbol call loop (~5763) and out of `receiverCallRelations` (~6484). Also leave them out of `topLevelBlock` masking (`js_scopes.go:393`, `provider.go:1817`). The whole-file component would otherwise blank all top-level script code. Do not add `component` to `typeLikeKind` (`types.go:12`).

## PR Sequence

PR0 comes first because the twins and scripts live only in a session scratchpad. PR7a is tiny and can land right after PR0.

### PR0: Land the Corpus and React Parity Reference (tests only)
- Commit `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/`: the README, both apps, `score.json`, and `vue_corpus_test.go`.
- Copy the React twins from the scratchpad (`scratchpad/twins/{taskboard-react,helpdesk-react}` with `twin-map.json`) into `testdata/vuecorpus/react/`.
- Port `scratchpad/tools/compare_twins.py` into `vue_corpus_test.go` as a parity score. It maps each fact by `.vue` → twin extension, `names`, and `no_counterpart`, and logs a `vue | react | comparable` column per tag. Ratchet only the Vue score.
- Add `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/` to `.graphignore` so the repo's own index is not polluted.

### PR7a: HTML-Id Regex (~+20 facts)
- `htmlEntitiesIdRe` (`parser.go:~4085`): require whitespace or `<` before `id`, and skip bound `:id`/`v-bind:id`.
- `.html` output changes too, so bump `IdentityRevision` and regenerate goldens.
- Gain: false-elements.

### PR1: Disclose Unmodeled Mentions in `impact`/`neighbors`
- New `internal/cli/inventory_mentions.go`, modeled on `value_refs.go`. It does a bounded whole-word scan for the symbol name in files whose header `LanguageTiers` tier is `inventory-only`. Vue is neither tier today (G), and after PR2 this covers Svelte and others.
- Register `W_INVENTORY_MENTIONS_UNMODELLED` in `diagnostic_scope.go:67`.
- Attach it in `impact` (~480) and to incoming `neighbors`. Render a line in `writeImpactFooter` (`internal/cli/impact_text.go:171`) via `completenessScope` (`internal/cli/completeness.go:34`), and add a JSON field (additive).
- Cap files and bytes, and disclose truncation.
- Tests: a Svelte fixture, plus a truncation test.

### PR2a: Parse Script Blocks (~450 lines, IdentityRevision 8 → 9)
- `vue.go` plus the parse seam above.
- `supportsSemanticExtraction` (`provider.go:882`): treat Vue as semantic, as SQL and Groovy are.
- `callExtractionLanguage` (`provider.go:1017`): include Vue. It is both the runtime gate and the capability report.
- Add `ooRelationSupport["Vue"]`: the TypeScript list without HANDLES_GRAPHQL and HANDLES_TRPC.
- Update `docs/language-support.md` and its counts, the `vue` entry in `language_matrix_test.go`, and the capability-union probe.
- Tests (`vue_test.go`):
  - The mask keeps byte length and newline positions.
  - Each `lang=` maps to its grammar; unknown `lang` falls back.
  - Existing component and element IDs are unchanged.
  - Parse errors carry file-relative lines.
  - Script symbols sit under the component.
- Gain: script-symbols, part of options-api, and component-owner CONTAINS.

### PR2b: Relation Seam (~500 lines; bump both cache versions)
- Relation seam items 1 to 7 above.
- Add a golden fixture `vue-basic`, then update `quality_coverage.json` and `TestCapabilityMatrixCoversEmittedRelations`.
- Assert that precomputed imports (`provider_parallel.go:221`, raw content) never apply to Vue once it is semantic.
- Free win to verify: Options API methods get the component as lexical container, so `this.save()` resolves through `methodsByContainer` (filled for any `method` with a container, ~5197) via `lookupMethodUpChain` (~8240).
- Gain: script-calls, options-api `this` calls.

### PR2c: Module Resolution (~200 lines) → corpus ~348
- Add a `jsImporterExtension` helper (JS-like or `.vue`). Do not widen `jsLikeExtension`, which feeds the Express and NestJS passes.
- Apply it at:
  - `isRelativeImportSpec` (~20884)
  - `resolveLocalImport` (~20900)
  - `resolveReadableLocalImport` (~20937)
  - `manifestImportResolver.resolve` (~22424)
  - `importedNamesFor` (~23985)
  - `importScanners` (~23698), for `.vue`
- In `jsModuleFiles` (~21416), key `.vue` files with the extension kept, so `TaskCard.ts` and `TaskCard.vue` don't collide and `@/components/X.vue` resolves through `resolveJSModulePath` (~22693).
- Gain: script-imports, path-alias (tsconfig).

### PR3a: Setup Attribution and Macro Types
- Make the component the `fileSource` for top-level `<script setup>` calls, mirroring `fsharpModuleInitBlock`.
- Emit USES_TYPE from the component for `defineProps<T>()`, `defineEmits<T>()`, and `withDefaults(defineProps<T>(), …)`, resolved through `importsByName`.
- Gain: component-owner CALLS, ts-types.

### PR3b: Options API and Mixins (~375 → ~412 with PR4)
- **Mixins and `extends`.** Add a Vue/JS-options case to `mixinSupertypeEdges` (`types.go:213`), next to the PHP/Ruby handling (`provider.go:~7079`, `buildMixinRelation`). It emits INHERITS from the component for `mixins: [a, b]` and EXTENDS for `extends: X`, resolved through imports.
- **`this` through mixins.** Add a Vue-only multi-parent lookup for `this.x()` into mixin members. The single-parent `superContainerByID` (~5294) does not fit.
- **Scope.** Options objects in plain `.js` (`export default {}` outside Vue) stay with the JS track.
- Gain: mixins, the rest of options-api.

### PR4a: Vue Events
- In Vue files only, a Vue variant of the channel scan:
  - `.$emit`, `emit(` from `defineEmits`, and `this.$emit` produce EMITS.
  - `.$on` and `.$once` produce LISTENS_ON.
  - `dispatch(` is excluded.
- Turn the channel scan back on for Vue with this variant. JS behavior of `emitCallRe` (`types.go:327`) stays unchanged.
- Gain: event-bus, and custom-event EMITS (13).

### PR4b: Vuex Strings
- `dispatch('ns/action')`, `commit('ns/MUTATION')`, `mapActions`/`mapGetters`/`mapMutations`, and the matching `this.x()` resolve to the module member.
- Read the namespace from the store root's `modules: {}` map.
- Emit CALLS at `pattern` resolution with evidence.
- Gain: store-members (the Vuex-string share only).

### PR7b: `<script src>`
- `<script src="./x.js">` emits IMPORTS from the `.vue` file.
- Gain: script-src.

## Out of Scope (File as Separate Issues)
- **Step 5, JS/TS track:**
  - multi-line imports and `webpackChunkName` comments in `scanJSImports`
  - aliased import names
  - `jsconfig.json`, tsconfig `references`, and comment stripping
  - const-bound factories in `callableTargetKind` and `@/` modules in `importedExternalSymbolName`
  - a `pair` case for arrow properties
  - member calls through returned and destructured objects
  - `localReachable` siblings and the same-name skip
  - false positives: `state` in `jsOpenParenStartsDeclarationOrControl`, `dispatch` in `emitCallRe`, bare `get(`/`post(` in `routingCallRe`
  - vitest and jest TESTS

  This is about +103 corpus facts, and the same gains for React.
- **Step 6, template and JSX edges** (+77): deferred. The design review recommends reusing CALLS from the component (Vue) or enclosing function (JSX), with a `template_binding` evidence kind and existing resolutions. A RENDERS type would need ADR 0001's namespaced `X-entire-graph:RENDERS`, a schema 1.7 minor, and a change in the `entire-brain` consumer. Global-registration edges depend on this step too.

## Verification
- **Per PR:** the unit tests listed above, the corpus ratchet with `-update` (review the gained-facts list in the diff), goldens and `quality_coverage.json` when they move, and `mise run check`.
- **Search regression (PR2a/b):** a query for a script function ranks the function above the whole-file component.
- **End to end after PR2c, and again after PR4b:**
  1. `go build -o /tmp/eg ./cmd/entire-graph`.
  2. Snapshot both corpus apps with `/tmp/eg snapshot --repo <app copy> --worktree --format ndjson`.
  3. In the taskboard copy, `/tmp/eg impact --repo . --symbol useTaskStore` lists Vue callers. In the helpdesk copy, `/tmp/eg neighbors --repo . --symbol fetchTickets --direction in` does the same.
  4. The parity column in `TestVueCorpusScore -v` shows Vue meeting or passing React on script-symbols, options-api, script-imports, script-calls, ts-types, component-owner, and mixins.
- **Target by milestone:** PR2c ~348, PR3b ~375, PR4b ~412, PR7a/b ~442 of 622.

# Vue Corpus

Two realistic Vue applications with a hand-written ground truth. Each app has an
`expected.json` that lists the symbols and relations a correct graph contains,
and tags every fact with the gap it measures. `vue_corpus_test.go` builds a
snapshot of each app, scores it against `expected.json`, and ratchets the
result in `score.json`, so every Vue improvement shows up as facts gained per
tag and every regression fails the test.

```sh
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus' -v            # score and compare
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -update  # record a new score
VUE_CORPUS_VERBOSE=1 go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -v  # list every missing fact
```

| App | Dialect |
|---|---|
| `taskboard/` | Vue 3, TypeScript, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia, vue-router, composables, `@/` path alias |
| `helpdesk/` | Options API, JavaScript, Vuex modules, mixins, event bus, global registration, kebab-case tags |

The apps are never built or run. They contain no `node_modules` or lockfiles,
and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.

input.command:
cat >> .graphignore <<'EOF'

# The Vue corpus is fixture apps (Vue, React, TypeScript, and JavaScript) that
# vue_corpus_test.go scores in its own temporary repos. It is test data, not
# this project's source, and would otherwise surface in searches of this repo.
internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/
EOF
python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''The apps are never built or run. They contain no `node_modules` or lockfiles,
and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.
'''
new='''The apps are never built or run. They contain no `node_modules` or lockfiles,
and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.

## React Twins

`react/taskboard/` and `react/helpdesk/` are the same apps in idiomatic React,
with the same files, names, and call paths. taskboard uses TSX function
components, zustand stores shaped like the Pinia stores, and react-router.
helpdesk uses JSX class components, Redux thunks named after the Vuex actions,
class inheritance in place of mixins, and the same event bus. They are the
parity target: they show what the provider already extracts for each construct
when it is written in a form the JavaScript engine understands.

Each twin's `twin-map.json` maps the Vue facts onto it:

```json
{"vue_ext": ".tsx", "files": {"src/router/index.ts": "src/router/index.tsx"},
 "names": {"src/views/X.vue#created": "componentDidMount"},
 "no_counterpart": {"<fact key>": "reason"}}
```

A `.vue` path maps to the twin extension unless `files` says otherwise, a
symbol keeps its name unless `names` renames it, and the Vue-only kinds
`component`, `document`, and `element` are dropped. `no_counterpart` lists facts
React has no equivalent for, such as custom-event channels, attribute traps,
and `<script src>`.

- `TestVueCorpusTwinsMapToSource` checks that every mapped endpoint names a twin
  file that declares the mapped name.
- `TestVueCorpusReactParity` logs, per tag, the Vue score, the React score on
  comparable facts, and the Vue score on those same facts. It is a report, not a
  ratchet.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace("go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus' -v            # score and compare",
            "go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus' -v            # score, compare, and print React parity")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
tail -5 .graphignore; grep -n "React Twins\|React parity" internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/README.md
